title: Choose the visual world
question: Bolder hand, steered to sans-serif and away from dim and bland. The deal put Data field first. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Data field
options.lineage: Ryoji Ikeda's datamatics: barcode fields and sine lattices
options.thesis: Pure black and white at data density; the masthead is a barcode field generated from the site's own content, and switching routes inverts it for one frame.
options.viewport: A full-width barcode band generated from the post history, the name in heavy grotesk cut out of it, then intro, links and experience as tight tabular columns.
options.case: Leads by deal order. Data-art is native to the audience; the monospace is translated to a sans grotesk per your steer, and the route accent is the only colour, used as the selection and inversion fill.
options.risk: Strobing and density can fight reading if the field leaks into articles; it must stay in the frame.

raised.raise: One module: an 8px unit sets every bar width, gap and column, so the field and the text share a grid.
Labels pin to what they describe by a hairline leader; nothing floats as a caption.
Photo plates share one scale and one baseline so the grid compares like a folio.

options.label: Spectral rail
options.lineage: Glass spectrograms on a viewing box
options.thesis: Everything hangs off one off-centre rail; colour exists only as bright emission lines, and each route owns one doubled line.
options.viewport: A spectrum band across the top with the route's line doubled; the name and intro hang right of an off-centre rail; experience is a time rail where the current role stands full height.
options.case: Reads more calmly than the field and holds clarity; spectroscopy is less native to programmers than data-art.
options.risk: The rail can feel like a gimmick if every element is forced onto it.

options.label: Monochrome product page
options.thesis: One neutral scale inverted to dark, one accent used four times, every claim followed by its proof.
options.viewport: Name and one-line claim, then intro paired with a proof panel of current work and stack, then experience as claim-proof rows.
options.case: Programmers know this look by heart (holds audience); it is also the closest to the standard you called bland.
options.risk: Polished but generic; little that is yours.

options.label: Brick build instructions
options.thesis: Numbered exploded steps on sky-blue pages.
options.viewport: Sky-blue spread with a big step numeral.
options.case: Sky-blue ground breaks the dark pin; wordless steps do not carry a profile.

options.label: Tensegrity column
options.thesis: Forces made visible on a pale concrete ground.
options.viewport: A breathing column with force labels.
options.case: Pale ground and a force-diagram layout replace reading order.

options.label: Botanical folio
options.thesis: One plant through five seasons on cream plates.
options.viewport: Five fixed-scale plates on one baseline.
options.case: Cream ground and italic serif break both pins.
options.kept: Plates share one scale and baseline.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The dark developer portfolio: centred column, name, bio, icon links, experience list.
canonCard.viewport: Name and one-line role, short bio, a row of icon links, then experience entries in soft cards.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from thousands of other developer sites by design.
